submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole fires on a prenominal modifier that identifies which instance, value or version of the head noun is meant - the determinative adjectives certain, specific, particular, given, specified, designated, predetermined, preset, predefined, fixed, default, desired, intended, requested, chosen, selected, arbitrary, same, different, respective - and not on the article, on demonstratives/quantifiers/ordinals (every 0.07, each 0.07, first 0.07, only 0.07, this 0.72, that 1.23, against 4.84 for 'a certain' in the same frame) or on ordinary descriptive adjectives in the identical slot (a large number 0.18, a blue car 0.02, a central angle 0.06, a long letter 0.06). It tracks that sense rather than the surface word or what follows it: 'a certain amount of time' peaks 9.48 on ' certain' but 'I am certain the ...' only 0.23, 'a fixed price' 2.55 but 'they fixed a price' 0.41, 'a given day' 5.32 but 'given the circumstances' 0.25, the negated 'unspecified' keeps only half (2.34 against 5.06), the token after the modifier is always at the floor (amount 0.00, direction 0.00, genre 0.00), and the negative pole never leaves zero, so the pole marks the identifying modifier itself and nothing downstream.

Visual attention to features by associative learning.
Expecting a particular stimulus can facilitate processing of that stimulus over others, but what is the fate of other stimuli that are known to co-occur with the expected stimulus? This study examined the impact of learned association on feature-based attention. The findings show that the effectiveness of an uninformative color transient in orienting attention can change by learned associations between colors and the expected target shape. In an initial acquisition phase, participants learned two distinct sequences of stimulus-response-outcome, where stimuli were defined by shape ('S' vs. 'H'), responses were localized key-presses (left vs. right), and outcomes were colors (red vs. green). Next, in a test phase, while expecting a target shape (80% probable), participants showed reliable attentional orienting to the color transient associated with the target shape, and showed no attentional orienting with the color associated with the alternative target shape. This bias seemed to be driven by learned association between shapes and colors, and not modulated by the response. In addition, the bias seemed to depend on observing target-color conjunctions, since encountering the two features disjunctively (without spatiotemporal overlap) did not replicate the findings. We conclude that associative learning - likely mediated by mechanisms underlying visual object representation - can extend the impact of goal-driven attention to features associated with a target stimulus.

Particularly, the steric wiring is indispensable to a high density mounting and, thus, various methods are being proposed in an attempt to manufacture a wiring board having a steric wiring. In general, the steric wirings are of a multi-layered structure such as a built-up wiring board prepared by laminating two dimensional printed wiring boards and a multi-layered wiring board. It is difficult to form a steric wiring having a free three dimensional shape. The built-up wiring board or the multi-layered wiring board has a structure that adjacent wiring layers are connected to each other by a conductive column called via. The via is formed by processing an insulating layer by a photolithography process using a photosensitive polyimide or resist, followed by selectively applying a plating to the via or by filling the via with a conductive paste. For forming a via by such a method, it is necessary to repeat a plurality of times the steps of resist coating, light exposure and etching, making the via formation highly laborious. In addition, it is difficult to improve the yield.
It is also possible to form the via by forming a through-hole (via hole) of a predetermined size in an insulating substrate constituting a printed wiring board by using a drill or a CO2 laser, followed by applying plating to the via hole or by filling the via hole with a conductive paste. In these methods, however, it is difficult to form freely a fine via having a size of scores of microns or less at a desired position.

title: On the norm of products of polynomials on ultraproducts of Banach spaces

Introduction
============

In this article we study the factor problem in the context of ultraproducts of Banach spaces. This problem can be stated as follows: for a Banach space $X$ over a field ${\mathbb K}$ (with ${\mathbb K}={\mathbb R}$ or ${\mathbb K}={\mathbb C}$) and natural numbers $k_1,\cdots, k_n$ find the optimal constant $M$ such that, given any set of continuous scalar polynomials $P_1,\cdots,P_n:X\rightarrow {\mathbb K}$, of degrees $k_1,\cdots,k_n$; the inequality $$\label{problema}
M \Vert P_1 \cdots P_n\Vert \ge  \, \Vert P_1 \Vert \cdots \Vert P_n \Vert$$ holds, where $\Vert P \Vert = \sup_{\Vert x \Vert_X=1} \vert P(x)\vert$. We also study a variant of the problem in which we require the polynomials to be homogeneous.

Recall that a function $P:X\rightarrow {\mathbb K}$ is a continuous $k-$homogeneous polynomial if there is a continuous $k-$linear function $T:X^k\rightarrow {\mathbb K}$ for which $P(x)=T(x,\cdots,x)$. A function $Q:X\rightarrow {\mathbb K}$ is a continuous polynomial of degree $k$ if $Q=\sum_{l=0}^k Q_l$ with $Q_0$ a constant, $Q_l$ ($1\leq l \leq k$) an $l-$homogeneous polynomial and $Q_k \neq 0$ .

October is finally in full swing, giving us four (count them: FOUR) movies in one week, one of which is the latest in supernatural horror: Sinister. Truth be told, this is a pretty solid horror movie overall, and gives a fresh spin on the idea of “found footage” movies! It’s brought to us by the producer of Paranormal Activity and Insidious, but doesn’t suffer from some of the issues that both of these had.

Paranormal Activity suffered from being regarded as either incredibly boring or weird and somewhat tense until everything comes to a head at the end. Insidious on the other hand, had a very strong and refreshingly scary feel to it that took a major nosedive in the third act. Sinister manages to maintain a consistent tone to its horror that builds over time…you know, like a proper movie should. It never quite reaches the heights of terror that either movie achieved when at their best, but is a strong effort that’s overall enjoyable.

Of all the characters involved, the most intriguing is easily Ellison Oswalt, played by Ethan Hawke. He’s a true crime writer with a desire to write his best book ever, and the desire quickly turns to an obsession, as the last time he achieved fame was a decade ago with his first book. This obsession drives him to not only move to the same town where the grisly deaths of a family occurred, but into their house where they were murdered!

Now it’s obvious that Sinister is a horror movie, but…the first act of the movie could very well be the first act of a crime thriller along the same lines as Red Dragon (a great movie that should be seen if you haven’t already). This provides the audience a good portrayal of the mental and physical toll that the story takes on Ellison, as well as the family dynamics and how his obsessions affect his wife and children.

Then again, my disappointment could be from comparing these kids to Pierce Gagnon, the kid from Looper.

Modulatory effects of PLG and its peptidomimetics on haloperidol-induced catalepsy in rats.
A behavioral model of dopaminergic function in the rat was used to examine the anticataleptic effects of L-prolyl-L-leucyl-glycinamide (PLG) and peptidomimetic analogs of PLG. Administration of 1 mg/kg PLG intraperitoneally significantly attenuated haloperidol (1 mg/kg)-induced catalepsy (as measured by the standard horizontal bar test), whereas doses of 0.1 and 10 mg/kg PLG did not. Eight synthetic PLG peptidomimetics (Calpha, alpha-dialkylated glycyl residues with lactam bridge constraint [1-4] and without [5-8]) were tested in the same manner (at a dose of 1 microg/kg) and categorized according to their activity, i.e. very active (5), moderately active (2, 3, 4, and 6), and inactive (1, 7, and 8). The catalepsy-reversal action of the diethylglycine-substituted peptidomimetic 5 was examined further and found to exhibit a U-shaped dose-response effect with an optimal dose of 1 microg/kg. The similarity between the effects of PLG and the synthetic peptidomimetics suggests a common mechanism of action. Finally, the synthetic peptidomimetics examined here, particularly peptidomimetic 5, were more effective than PLG in attenuating haloperidol-induced catalepsy.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I am certain the parcel arrived on Thursday, though the tracking page still shows it in transit.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests 'certain' in its epistemic predicate sense, where it expresses confidence rather than identifying which instance of the head noun is meant, so the hypothesis predicts it stays inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Certain of the outcome, she boarded the train without a backward glance.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Puts 'certain' in a fronted predicative phrase at the very start of the probe, testing both the non-determinative sense and an unusual position that the hypothesis says should not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: A technician fixed the leaking valve in the basement and charged us for two hours of labour.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests 'fixed' as a past-tense verb rather than a prenominal modifier, the same contrast the hypothesis draws with 'they fixed a price'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Given the icy conditions, the school bus will not run this morning.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests 'given' as a sentence-initial preposition introducing circumstances, which the hypothesis predicts is inactive because it does not select an instance of the following noun.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The audit, and in particular its treatment of travel expenses, drew sharp criticism from the board.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests 'particular' inside the fixed adverbial 'in particular', where it is not a prenominal identifier of a head noun.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: To be specific, the clinic closes at four on Fridays and stays shut all weekend.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests 'specific' as a sentence adverbial with no noun for it to identify, a use absent from the top examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Any visitor who arrives after six must sign the register at the front desk.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests a quantifier determiner in the same prenominal slot the hypothesis reserves for identifying modifiers, so it predicts the floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: A heated argument broke out over the parking policy at the residents' meeting.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests a participial descriptive adjective in the identical 'a ___ noun' frame, which the hypothesis says is at the floor like 'a blue car'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Borrowers who default on the loan will forfeit the collateral within thirty days.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests 'default' as a verb, not as a prenominal modifier naming which version applies.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The winner was chosen by a panel of three judges after a long deliberation.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests the claimed trigger 'chosen' inside a passive verb phrase rather than in the prenominal position the hypothesis says carries the feature.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: My script splits each line on every comma, so rows containing quoted fields break and the third column lands in the wrong place. I have read the documentation twice and still cannot see why this happens.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Matches the programming-help genre of two top examples but contains only quantifiers, an ordinal and descriptive vocabulary, so the hypothesis predicts no identifying modifier fires.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Enter the exact amount shown on your invoice into the box marked Total.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Paraphrase holdout: 'exact' picks out which value is meant, the claimed sense expressed with a word absent from the trigger list and from the top examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The relevant paragraph of the agreement is reproduced in Appendix B for reference.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Paraphrase holdout in a contract genre: 'relevant' selects which paragraph is meant using a word the hypothesis does not list, testing the sense rather than the surface form.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
Section 4.2 Pre-flight inspection. Before each departure the first officer walks around the aircraft and confirms that every panel latch sits flush, that the static ports are clear of ice, and that no bird-strike damage is visible along the leading edges. The walk-around takes about ten minutes in good weather and considerably longer when the apron is covered with slush. Maintenance records from the previous sector are reviewed in the crew room, and any deferred item is discussed with the engineer on duty. Fuel is ordered for the next sector while the aircraft is still on stand, and the dispatcher sends the final load figures to the flight deck about twenty minutes before departure. If those figures change after that point, the crew must recalculate the take-off performance before requesting pushback. The captain then checks the fuel figure against the load sheet, signs the technical log, and confirms that the cargo doors have been closed and locked. Passengers board through the forward door while the cabin crew demonstrates the safety brief. Once the doors are armed, the flight deck runs the before-start checklist item by item. Engine start is normally quiet; the second engine spools up a few seconds after the first. Taxi clearance is requested from ground control, and the crew reads back the routing to the holding point.

During the take-off roll the pilot flying calls out airspeed at eighty knots, and the pilot monitoring cross-checks the engine instruments against the predetermined limits printed on the placard beside the throttle quadrant. Rotation begins at the rotation speed, and the aircraft climbs away on the runway heading until the departure procedure is authorised. In the cruise the crew monitors the weather ahead, and any deviation from track is coordinated with the controller before it is flown. Descent preparation starts about forty minutes before landing, when the crew obtains the destination weather and reviews the approach brief. The landing checklist is completed before descending below a thousand feet, and the aircraft is configured for landing with flaps set as required.

After the aircraft has parked and the passengers have disembarked, the crew completes the post-flight walk-around and records any defects in the technical log. Crew duty limits are tracked by the operator, and the roster for the following week is published every Thursday. Any change to a published roster needs the agreement of both pilots and is recorded in the operations manual. Rest periods away from base are counted from the moment the crew reaches the hotel, not from the moment the aircraft parks, a distinction that has caused more than one dispute with the scheduling office. Training records, medical certificates and licence renewals are held electronically and audited once a year by the regulator.

explanation_scores.explanation: This pole fires on a prenominal modifier that identifies which instance, value or version of the head noun is meant - the determinative adjectives certain, specific, particular, given, specified, designated, predetermined, preset, predefined, fixed, default, desired, intended, requested, chosen, selected, arbitrary, same, different, respective - and not on the article, on demonstratives/quantifiers/ordinals (every 0.07, each 0.07, first 0.07, only 0.07, this 0.72, that 1.23, against 4.84 for 'a certain' in the same frame) or on ordinary descriptive adjectives in the identical slot (a large number 0.18, a blue car 0.02, a central angle 0.06, a long letter 0.06). It tracks that sense rather than the surface word or what follows it: 'a certain amount of time' peaks 9.48 on ' certain' but 'I am certain the ...' only 0.23, 'a fixed price' 2.55 but 'they fixed a price' 0.41, 'a given day' 5.32 but 'given the circumstances' 0.25, the negated 'unspecified' keeps only half (2.34 against 5.06), the token after the modifier is always at the floor (amount 0.00, direction 0.00, genre 0.00), and the negative pole never leaves zero, so the pole marks the identifying modifier itself and nothing downstream.
